name: spatio-flux-test-suite
title: Spatio-Flux Test Suite — compositional multiscale scenarios
biological_story:
Metabolism, spatial transport, and particle dynamics coupled on a shared
lattice reproduce COMETS-style spatial dFBA and particle–field exchange: cells
consume and secrete metabolites into diffusing extracellular fields, and
particle populations advect and react on the same grid.

executive.what_is_this: The spatio-flux reference application as one investigation, in two layers: (1) 19 reproduction studies that faithfully re-run every scenario of the original test suite as a hardened, quantitatively code-evaluated baseline; and (2) biology-forward studies that extend those composites into new emergent biology — a spatial cross-feeding partnership and a settling biofilm — plus a zero-carbon adversarial control.
executive.verdict: SpatioFlux resolves emergent spatial biology its well-mixed constituents cannot. In spatial_cross_feeding_bridge, a producer strain growing on glucose secretes acetate that diffuses across the lattice to a consumer strain on the no-glucose side, which grows only on that bridge — and an A-absent control produces no acetate and no consumer growth, so the partnership is real, not incidental. In biofilm_settling_metabolism, rigid-body cells settle and pack under gravity while feeding, so per-cell growth becomes spatially structured by depth — mechanics and metabolism couple. A zero-carbon adversarial control correctly shows no growth, establishing these signals as carbon-driven biology rather than artifacts. Underneath, all 19 original composition scenarios still pass their regression plus new quantitative contracts — the reproduction baseline the new biology is built on.

scientific_argument.main_claim: Independently developed processes (dFBA, Monod kinetics, diffusion-advection, Brownian and Newtonian particles) compose through typed shared state into quantitatively measurable emergent spatial biology — a diffusion-bridged cross-feeding partnership between spatially separated strains, and a gravity-settled biofilm whose growth is structured by depth — each asserted by a code-evaluated contract on a real run, not by artifact existence alone.
scientific_argument.support: The DAG (standalone → pairs → triples → reference demos) is documentation of composition order, not an execution gate — every study runs independently and its output is checked against the out0 oracle, so a passing combination is evidence the constituent processes compose without hidden coupling.
evidence_for: spatial_cross_feeding_bridge: strain B's biomass overlaps the diffused acetate field more than glucose, strain A grows and secretes the acetate bridge, and the A-absent control leaves B flat — an emergent spatial cross-feeding partnership.

biofilm_settling_metabolism: rigid-body cells settle under gravity (mean depth increases) and per-cell mass correlates with depth while the population grows — mechanics-coupled, depth-structured metabolic growth.
19 reproduction studies: every original composition scenario passes its regression check plus a new quantitative growth / depletion / mass-conservation / MSD contract.
nutrient_starvation_control (adversarial): with zero glucose the model does not grow, establishing the growth signals as carbon-driven, not solver artifacts.
evidence_against: The novel signals are modest in magnitude (acetate is a poor carbon source; the biofilm depth-structuring is weak at a few cells) and the particle studies are stochastic (biofilm uses a seeded, reproducible run).
Single lattice/parameterization and horizon; reduced/core dFBA models.
caveats: Claims are evaluated at the simulated horizons/resolutions; a washout (Péclet) survival transition was attempted but did not appear (per-site dFBA growth outpaced transport) and is deferred as a follow-up.

competing_frameworks.name: Well-mixed ODE / batch metabolism
competing_frameworks.relation: SpatioFlux resolves the spatial structure these omit — e.g. spatial_cross_feeding_bridge shows a consumer growing only on a producer's diffused metabolite, which a well-mixed model cannot represent.

competing_frameworks.name: Field-only COMETS spatial dFBA
competing_frameworks.relation: complementary and reproduced here (comets_* studies); SpatioFlux additionally couples particle-based (agent) biomass to the fields.

competing_frameworks.name: Particle-based vs field-based biomass
competing_frameworks.relation: both are expressed in the composites; the particle (br_/comets_br_/reference) and field (comets_diffusion/spatial_*) studies compare the two representations of the same growth.

studies.name: monod_kinetics
studies.question: Field-only baseline: Monod uptake/growth on a well-mixed substrate pool (no spatial lattice, no particles). Use to sanity-check kinetics + mass balance.

findings.statement: spatio_flux reproduces the monod_kinetics test-suite artifacts and the composite's structural schema matches its committed reference.
Biomass grows monotonically and glucose is driven to near-zero, the field-only Monod growth signature.

studies.claim: Monod uptake kinetics drive biomass growth and near-complete glucose depletion in a well-mixed pool.

derived.insight: spatio_flux reproduces the monod_kinetics test-suite artifacts and the composite's structural schema matches its committed reference.

studies.name: diffusion_process

Total glucose and total dissolved biomass are conserved to numerical precision across the run — the finite-volume transport neither creates nor destroys mass, only moves it.

studies.claim: Finite-volume transport conserves total field mass (closed boundaries) while redistributing the seeded biomass band.

derived.insight: spatio_flux reproduces the diffusion_process test-suite artifacts and the composite's structural schema matches its committed reference.

studies.name: brownian_particles
studies.question: Particle-only baseline: Brownian motion of agents with mass in continuous space (no fields, no metabolism). Checks integrator + particle state schema.

findings.statement: spatio_flux reproduces the brownian_particles test-suite artifacts and the composite's structural schema matches its committed reference.

The agents' mean-squared displacement grows with a positive slope over the run (net diffusive spreading) and the population count is non-decreasing. Few-particle Brownian runs are noisy, so this is a spreading check, not a strict MSD-linearity claim (single runs vary in slope and fit quality).

studies.claim: Mass-carrying agents undergo diffusive Brownian motion — mean-squared displacement grows linearly in time — while the population seeds in.

derived.insight: spatio_flux reproduces the brownian_particles test-suite artifacts and the composite's structural schema matches its committed reference.

studies.name: nutrient_starvation_control
studies.title: Nutrient-starvation negative control
studies.question: With no carbon source, does the dynamic-FBA model correctly fail to grow — the falsification control that the growth signal is real, not an artifact?

resolved: Growth requires a carbon source; with none, the model correctly produces no biomass.
remaining: Other falsification controls (e.g. zero-oxygen, blocked uptake) could further bound the growth claim.

followup_study_proposals.motivation: A carbon-present-but-uptake-blocked control would separate 'no substrate' from 'no uptake capacity' as causes of no growth.
followup_study_proposals.candidate: ecoli_core_dfba with a clamped/knocked-out glucose exchange

findings.statement: With no carbon source the cell does not grow — biomass is flat within noise. This adversarial control passes by REJECTING growth, establishing that the biomass increases throughout the investigation are carbon-driven biology, not a solver artifact.

studies.claim: With zero glucose the dynamic-FBA cell does not grow: biomass stays flat within noise. The growth seen in every other study is therefore carbon-driven, not a numerical artifact — this negative control passes by rejecting growth.

derived.insight: With no carbon source the cell does not grow — biomass is flat within noise. This adversarial control passes by REJECTING growth, establishing that the biomass increases throughout the investigation are carbon-driven biology, not a solver artifact.

studies.name: spatial_cross_feeding_bridge
studies.title: Spatial cross-feeding bridge
studies.question: Does a spatially-separated consumer (strain B) grow only where a producer (strain A) secretes a diffusing metabolite?

resolved: A spatially-separated consumer grows only on a producer's diffused metabolite — spatial cross-feeding.
remaining: Two further spatial phenomena are deferred: strain demixing/sectoring at an expanding front, and an advection washout transition (the latter did not appear — per-site dFBA growth outpaced transport at feasible advection; it needs a non-growing tracer or a much slower-growth regime).

followup_study_proposals.motivation: Cross-feeding shows spatial metabolic coupling between separated strains; a complementary question is whether competing strains demix into sectors at a growing colony front. Needs strain-tagged particles (strain_particle type) + a dense front.
followup_study_proposals.candidate: comets_br_particles_dfba with two strain-tagged founder populations

followup_study_proposals.motivation: A washout/Peclet survival transition did not appear with growing per-site dFBA (growth always outpaced outflow transport). Revisit with a non-growing biomass tracer or a slow-growth regime so advection can win.
followup_study_proposals.candidate: comets_washout with a non-growing tracer / reduced growth rate

findings.statement: Strain B grows only when strain A is present to secrete acetate: with A, B's biomass overlaps the diffused acetate field and increases modestly (~1.6%); with A absent, no acetate forms and B stays flat. The A-absent control is the decisive evidence that the small increment is A's acetate bridge, not residual glucose or incidental growth. The magnitude is small (acetate is a poor carbon source) — the claim is about the spatial dependency, not the yield.

studies.claim: Strain A grows on glucose and secretes acetate that diffuses to strain B on the no-glucose side, producing a small, acetate-dependent growth increment in B that does not occur when A is absent — an emergent, spatially-localized cross-feeding dependency (the effect is modest: B grows ~1.6% over the run).

derived.insight: Strain B grows only when strain A is present to secrete acetate: with A, B's biomass overlaps the diffused acetate field and increases modestly (~1.6%); with A absent, no acetate forms and B stays flat. The A-absent control is the decisive evidence that the small increment is A's acetate bridge, not residual glucose or incidental growth. The magnitude is small (acetate is a poor carbon source) — the claim is about the spatial dependency, not the yield.

studies.name: biofilm_settling_metabolism
studies.title: Biofilm settling + metabolism
studies.question: When rigid-body cells settle under gravity while feeding, does growth become spatially structured by depth?

resolved: Gravity-driven settling + feeding produce a growing, packed biofilm layer (mechanics coupled to metabolism).
remaining: Whether growth is structured by depth is unresolved — needs many more cells, multiseed, and deterministic (pymunk-seeded) runs to establish a reproducible correlation.

followup_study_proposals.motivation: Establish (or refute) depth-structured growth with a seeded, multiseed, higher-cell-count sweep so the correlation is reproducible and significant.

findings.statement: Rigid-body cells settle under gravity (mean depth drops) and feed, and the population grows and divides — a physics-coupled settling biofilm that the field-only metabolism studies cannot show. Whether growth is additionally structured by depth is an open question: the mass-vs-depth correlation is weak (~0.4) and not reproducible at this cell count.

studies.claim: Rigid-body cells settle and pack under gravity while feeding on the nutrient field, and the population grows — a physics-coupled settling biofilm. Whether per-cell growth is structured by depth is suggestive but NOT established at this scale (the mass-vs-depth correlation is weak, ~0.4, not significant at ~10 cells, and varies run to run).

derived.insight: Rigid-body cells settle under gravity (mean depth drops) and feed, and the population grows and divides — a physics-coupled settling biofilm that the field-only metabolism studies cannot show. Whether growth is additionally structured by depth is an open question: the mass-vs-depth correlation is weak (~0.4) and not reproducible at this cell count.
